name: @didit-protocol/mcp-server

tools.name: didit_account_register
tools.description: Register a new Didit account. A 6-character verification code is sent to the email. Follow up with didit_account_verify_email.

password.description: Password (min 8 chars, must include uppercase, lowercase, digit, special char)

tools.name: didit_account_verify_email
tools.description: Verify email with the 6-character code. Returns the new organization with its live application and its sandbox_application (each with client_id and api_key) and an access_token, and signs the local server in: the tools that follow are authenticated automatically. If the account already has two-factor authentication it returns 2fa_required (and a temp_token when it has an authenticator) instead of tokens: finish with didit_account_verify_2fa. If the account's organization enforces SSO it returns sso_required: no token or API key is issued here, so ask the person to sign in through their organization's SSO in the Didit console in a browser; do not retry.

tools.name: didit_account_resend_otp
tools.description: Resend the 6-character email verification code for a pending registration. Codes expire after 10 minutes.

email.description: Email address the code was originally sent to

tools.name: didit_account_login
tools.description: Log in to an existing Didit account. Signs the local server in, so the tools that follow are authenticated automatically, and returns access_token. If the account has two-factor authentication it returns 2fa_required and a temp_token instead: finish with didit_account_verify_2fa. If the account's organization enforces SSO it returns sso_required: no token is issued by password, so ask the person to sign in through SSO in the console, or use didit_account_device_login_start. For an account that signs in with a passkey or SSO (no password), use didit_account_device_login_start instead.

tools.name: didit_account_device_login_start
tools.description: Sign in WITHOUT a password or local browser (OAuth device code): returns a short user_code and a URL the person opens on any device to approve this connection. Works for passkey and SSO accounts. Then call didit_account_device_login_poll. Credentials are stored locally and used automatically afterwards.

tools.name: didit_account_device_login_poll
tools.description: Wait (up to about 45 seconds) for the person to approve the sign-in started with didit_account_device_login_start. Returns status pending (call again) or connected with the granted scope.

tools.name: didit_account_verify_2fa
tools.description: Finish logging in to an account with two-factor authentication, using the temp_token from didit_account_login and the current 6-digit authenticator code (or an unused backup code). Signs the local server in, like didit_account_login, and returns access_token.

temp_token.description: temp_token returned by didit_account_login (valid for 5 minutes)

code.description: 6-digit code from the authenticator app, or an unused backup code

tools.name: didit_org_list
tools.description: List the organizations you belong to (each has an id to pass as organization_id to other tools). In hosted OAuth mode no arguments are needed. In stdio mode the sign-in from login/verify_email is used automatically.

access_token.description: Only for stdio mode, and only to act as another account than the one signed in: a Bearer access token from login/verify_email.

tools.name: didit_org_list_applications
tools.description: List the applications in an organization (each has an id to pass as application_id). In hosted OAuth mode pass only organization_id.

organization_id.description: Organization UUID (from didit_org_list)

access_token.description: Only for stdio mode. Omit in hosted OAuth mode.

tools.name: didit_org_get_application
tools.description: Get application details (client_id etc.). The api_key is REDACTED — a masked preview + api_key_set flag are returned, never the raw secret.

access_token.description: Only for stdio mode. Omit in hosted OAuth mode.

tools.name: didit_org_reveal_application_api_key
tools.description: Return the RAW, un-redacted api_key for an application. This exposes a LIVE SECRET — only call when a human explicitly needs the key to integrate; never log or persist it. Requires confirm:true AND an explicit organization_id + application_id (no defaults).

organization_id.description: REQUIRED. No env/context default for this raw-secret tool.

application_id.description: REQUIRED. No env/context default for this raw-secret tool.

confirm.description: REQUIRED. Must be true to expose the raw key. Only set after explicit user confirmation of this exact action.

tools.name: didit_context_get
tools.description: Return ALL organizations you can access with their applications nested, plus the default org/app when unambiguous — in ONE call (replaces didit_org_list + per-org didit_org_list_applications). Call this first to discover ids.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

tools.description: Aggregate verification analytics ACROSS ALL your apps and organizations in one call - the efficient way to answer questions like "how many people tried phone verification but dropped off in the last 15 days?". Returns summed status counts (request_breakdown), a feature_funnel (how many sessions REACHED each step: OCR, LIVENESS, FACE_MATCH, AML, POA, PHONE, EMAIL, ...), warning_stats by risk code, the previous period's request_breakdown, per-workflow session totals and a recomputed conversion_rate, for a date window. Omit organization_id/application_id to span everything; pass them to narrow.

last_n_days.description: Relative window: include only the last N days (sets date_from/date_to). Alternative to passing date_from/date_to.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

tools.name: didit_session_create
tools.description: Create a verification session. Requires workflow_id (created in the Console Workflows page) — the workflow defines which steps run and whether the session is KYC or KYB. Returns session_id, url, and session_token.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

workflow_id.description: REQUIRED. The STABLE workflow_id (`workflow_id` of didit_workflow_search/list) of the workflow that defines the verification steps; runs its live version. A version uuid pins that one version and ignores later publishes. Selects KYC vs KYB implicitly.

vendor_data.description: Your unique identifier for the user (e.g. user ID). Used to group sessions into a user/business.

callback.description: URL to redirect the user to after verification

callback_method.description: Which device/flow the callback applies to

language.description: Pre-set the verification UI language (ISO code)

sandbox_scenario.description: SANDBOX ONLY (an application whose mode is 'sandbox' — see didit_context_get): predefine the outcome instead of running real providers, so the session is never billed. Slugs are 'approve', 'decline_*' (e.g. decline_aml_hit, decline_document_expired, decline_kyb_registry_mismatch) and 'review_*' (e.g. review_aml_possible_match). Ignored by a live application, where every session IS billed.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON stored on the session and echoed in webhooks

contact_details.description: Pre-fill contact info (e.g. email, phone) for the session

expected_details.description: Expected values to validate against (e.g. expected country, IP)

portrait_image.description: Base64 or URL reference portrait for Biometric Authentication / Face-Match-first workflows. Optional when the vendor_data user already has a stored face (approved liveness face, ePassport photo, document portrait, or enrolled profile face) - the stored face is reused automatically; 400 if neither is available

tools.name: didit_session_list
tools.description: List verification sessions for ONE app. If you have multiple apps (or pass no scope) this automatically spans every app, newest first - but didit_session_search is the canonical cross-app tool and what to reach for to answer "my last N sessions". HOW MANY: `count` stops at 100 (100 means "100 or more"); when it does, the result adds `total_count` (the exact number, from the console's own tab counts) or `count_is_lower_bound: true`. Answer "how many" from total_count, never report 100 as the number; limit:1 is enough to count.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

status.description: Filter by session status (Not Started, In Progress, In Review, Approved, Declined, Expired, Abandoned, Kyc Expired, Resubmitted, Awaiting User). Several statuses separated by commas match any of them, e.g. "Not Started,In Progress".

search.description: Free-text search. S-<number> finds a session by number exactly.

tools.name: didit_session_get_decision
tools.description: Get the full verification decision and all extracted data for a session.

tools.name: didit_session_get_location_evidence
tools.description: Precise Location (GEOLOCATION) evidence of ONE session, per Location node: `config` (what judged it, every action resolved through the preset), `result` (the decision's verdict), EVERY attempt incl. retired ones (`retired:true`), `reference_points` (device, IP, address; `area_reading` is the earlier attempt a carried area verdict stands on), `distances`, `areas` (inside / blocked / undetermined area ids, `nearest_allowed_km`, `allowed_result`), `anonymizers` (vpn, proxy, tor, spoofing, emulator; null = cannot tell) and `history`: the same person's earlier checks (same vendor_data) that LOCATION_CONSECUTIVE_MISMATCHES and travel tolerance are judged from. The decision keeps only the accepted attempt: use this for 'which attempt was outside', 'why consecutive mismatches' or 'why was the distance excused'. Holds precise coordinates: quote only what the question needs. `nodes: []` means no Location attempt was recorded; a 404 'Precise Location is not available.' means the feature is off on this deployment.

tools.name: didit_session_simulate
tools.description: SANDBOX ONLY: finish a session of a sandbox application (mode 'sandbox' in didit_context_get) with the outcome you pick, without anyone going through the verification flow, then read it with didit_session_get_decision and its webhooks with didit_session_webhooks. Never billed. Pass new_status ('Approved', 'Declined', 'In Review', 'Expired', 'Abandoned'), a scenario slug ('approve', 'decline_aml_hit', 'decline_document_expired', 'review_aml_possible_match', ...) or a risk. A live session answers not found.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. A session of a sandbox application.

scenario.description: Sandbox scenario slug whose outcome to reproduce.

risk.description: A risk case to add as a warning.

send_webhooks.description: Send the webhooks a real status change sends (default true).

tools.name: didit_session_update_status
tools.description: Overwrite a session's decision by approving, declining, or requesting resubmission; optionally send a notification email that cannot be recalled. Before calling, obtain explicit user confirmation of the session, new decision, and any email recipient. For resubmission, pass new_status='Resubmitted' and nodes_to_resubmit; already-approved steps are kept.

comment.description: Reviewer note stored on the audit trail

nodes_to_resubmit.description: Node IDs the user must redo (only for Resubmitted)

send_email.description: Send a notification email that cannot be recalled. Set true only after explicit user confirmation of the notification and recipient.

email_address.description: Override the notification recipient; confirm this address with the user before sending.

tools.name: didit_session_update_data
tools.description: Correct the KYC data extracted from the ID document on a session (reviewer override). Only send the fields you want to change.

tools.name: didit_session_update_poa_data
tools.description: Correct the Proof of Address data extracted from the POA document on a session (reviewer override). Only send the fields you want to change.

tools.name: didit_session_delete
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly delete a single verification session (KYC or KYB) - its verification data and stored media. Blocklist entries, issued share tokens, already-queued webhook deliveries, consumed credits, and the parent user/business are not affected. Requires confirm:true - only pass it after the user has explicitly confirmed this exact deletion.

confirm.description: REQUIRED. Must be true - deletion is permanent and irreversible. Only set after explicit user confirmation of this exact action.

tools.name: didit_session_batch_delete
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly delete multiple KYC sessions by session number, or EVERY KYC session in the application with delete_all:true (KYB sessions are never touched; delete those individually). Requires confirm:true - only pass it after the user has explicitly confirmed this exact deletion.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_numbers.description: Array of session numbers to delete

delete_all.description: Set true to delete ALL sessions (ignores session_numbers)

confirm.description: REQUIRED. Must be true - deletion is permanent and irreversible. Only set after explicit user confirmation of this exact action.

tools.name: didit_session_generate_pdf
tools.description: Return download_url, expires_at and expires_in (300 seconds) for the original Didit session PDF. Fetch the URL to save the PDF; no Authorization header is needed. Treat the URL as sensitive. Requires configured MCP HTTP PDF downloads.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

tools.name: didit_session_get_signature_evidence
tools.description: Return download_url, content_type, expires_at and expires_in (300 seconds) for a signer's evidence PDF of an E-signature step: level and format, signer, IP address, each document with its original SHA-256 and field values and the SHA-256 of every signed file, plus, for an Advanced (AES) signature, the verified identity session, the code confirmation, the certificate and the timestamp. Pass the evidence_file path's signer as signature_id; a Business Verification step with several signers needs it, otherwise the route picks one. Fetch the URL to save the PDF; no Authorization header is needed. Treat the URL as sensitive. Requires configured MCP HTTP downloads (see the README).

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session.

node_id.description: REQUIRED. The E-signature step: node_id of the item in the decision's signatures[].

signature_id.description: id of the signer's item in signatures[]. Required to pick a signer on a Business Verification step with several.

tools.name: didit_session_get_signed_document
tools.description: Return download_url, content_type, expires_at and expires_in (300 seconds) for the signed PDF of one document of an E-signature step: the document the signer was shown with their field values stamped and the evidence page (unless signature_evidence_page is off). An Advanced (AES) PDF also carries the PAdES signature with its timestamp; a Simple PDF has no digital signature, seal or timestamp. Didit checks the file against sha256_signed first (409 on a mismatch, nothing returned). Use the id of the document in signatures[].documents[]. Treat the URL as sensitive. Requires configured MCP HTTP downloads.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session.

node_id.description: REQUIRED. The E-signature step: node_id of the item in the decision's signatures[].

document_id.description: REQUIRED. id of the document in signatures[].documents[].

tools.name: didit_session_get_signature_field_image
tools.description: Return download_url, content_type (image/png), expires_at and expires_in (300 seconds) for the signature or initials a signer applied to a field. Use the field id from the image_url of signatures[].documents[].fields[]. Treat the URL as sensitive. Requires configured MCP HTTP downloads.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session.

node_id.description: REQUIRED. The E-signature step: node_id of the item in the decision's signatures[].

field_id.description: REQUIRED. The field on this signer's copy, as in the field's image_url.

tools.name: didit_session_validate_signatures
tools.description: Re-check the signed documents of an E-signature step and save the result in each signer's validation. Didit re-reads every signed PDF, checks its SHA-256 and, for an Advanced (AES) signature, validates the PAdES signature, the certificate, the revocation data and the timestamp (a Simple signature has no digital signature, so only file integrity is checked). Nothing is signed again. Without signature_id every signer of the step is checked and the call fails with 409 if any has not signed; 400 means a stored signed PDF no longer matches its recorded SHA-256. Returns the checked signers.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session.

node_id.description: REQUIRED. The E-signature step: node_id of the item in the decision's signatures[].

signature_id.description: id of one signer's item in signatures[]; omit to check every signer of the step.

tools.description: List the review history and activity log for a session, newest first. One page: 50 entries unless `limit` says otherwise, with `count` as the total and `offset` to read the ones after.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

limit.description: How many to return in this call (1 to 200). `count` in the answer is the total.

offset.description: How many to skip: pass the number you have already read to get the ones after them.

tools.name: didit_session_add_review
tools.description: Add a review note to a session's audit trail, optionally changing its status.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

new_status.description: Optional new session status to record with the note

tools.name: didit_session_share
tools.description: Share a verified session with a trusted partner for reusable KYC (B2B session sharing).

tools.name: didit_session_explain_decision
tools.description: WHY a verification session ended Approved / Declined / In Review, as a deterministic trace read from the record: the feature that decided it (strictest wins), each warning that had an effect with its raw value, every triggered status rule (field, operator, configured vs actual value), the human override if a reviewer changed the automatic verdict, and for each cause the workflow config key that governs it (`lever`, with its CURRENT value read from the workflow graph; only keys that exist in the feature-config contract; null means it is not a workflow setting). `workflow.graph_read:false` means the graph could not be read, so no current values. Use this for every 'why was it declined / in review / approved', 'it should have been X' and 'how do I make these go to X' question INSTEAD of reading the whole decision — it never returns images, extracted fields or PII. `informational` lists warnings that changed nothing. `unexplained:true` means a decided session (Declined / In Review) whose record shows no effective cause (e.g. minimized age-assurance logs): say so, never invent one. `lifecycle_status:true` (Expired, Abandoned, Not Started, In Progress, Resub Requested…) means nothing decided it — the status is the whole explanation.

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The session uuid (from the page's session-id param, didit_session_search or the user)

tools.name: didit_session_webhooks
tools.description: Delivery log of the webhooks Didit sent for ONE session (last 30 days): destination URL, HTTP response status, timing, signing headers (X-Signature/X-Timestamp) and a capped copy of the payload. The way to check an integration end to end: create a session on a SANDBOX application with sandbox_scenario 'approve' (unbilled, fires status.updated immediately), then call this with wait_seconds so the call waits for the delivery instead of you polling. A 2xx response_status means the customer's endpoint received it; 401/403 usually means their signature check (must be HMAC-SHA256 hex of the RAW body); an empty list after the wait means the endpoint never got the event (not public, or the destination is disabled).

session_id.description: REQUIRED. The session whose deliveries to read

wait_seconds.description: Keep polling up to this many seconds until at least one delivery exists (0 = read once). Use 30-45 right after creating a sandbox session.

tools.name: didit_session_webhook_resend
tools.description: Resend one recorded webhook delivery of a session to the configured endpoint (the session page's own Resend). Use after the customer fixed their endpoint so they do not need a new session; returns the new delivery with its response_status.

webhook_id.description: REQUIRED. The delivery's uuid from didit_session_webhooks

tools.name: didit_session_import_shared
tools.description: Import a shared verification session from a partner (Reusable KYC).

share_token.description: Token received from the sharing partner

tools.name: didit_session_create_import
tools.description: Create a bulk import job: a hosted CSV/NDJSON file (source_file_url) of historical verifications, or (source=provider) a migration from another identity verification provider. File imports use Didit's canonical schema; label a record's source with the optional per-row `provider` column in the file. A provider migration reads Sumsub, Onfido, Persona and ComplyCube with the customer's READ-ONLY key (`credentials`, named as that provider's credential_fields from didit_session_list_import_providers); Veriff, iDenfy and MetaMap are read by the record IDs in source_file_url, and the others import an export file. The key is secret: ask the user for a read-only key, never log or repeat it, and never reuse it. Didit encrypts it, never returns it and erases it when the import ends. Prefer dry_run:true first: it counts what would import and writes nothing, ends READY, and didit_session_manage_import action=start then imports for real. Record IDs are namespaced by provider, so re-runs and moving between a file and a provider migration never import a record twice. An application runs at most 4 active import jobs at once (a fifth answers 429); a job a deploy interrupted resumes by itself. Imports must be enabled for the organization by Didit and are refused on a sandbox application (403).

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

source_file_url.description: Publicly fetchable HTTPS URL of the CSV/NDJSON file (or, for providers read by record IDs, of the ID list) to import.

source_format.description: File format (default: inferred from the URL)

workflow_id.description: Workflow to associate imported sessions with

source.description: provider makes this a migration from another provider. Omit for a file import.

provider.description: Migration source id from didit_session_list_import_providers (for example sumsub, onfido, persona). Required when source is provider.

credentials.description: SECRET. The provider's read-only key, with the field names its credential_fields list. Never echo it back to the user or into logs.

options.description: Provider options, for example { region } (Onfido: eu, us, ca).

status_mapping.description: Edits to the provider's default status mapping: source status to Didit status. Not Finished and Abandoned are skipped and counted, never imported.

dry_run.description: Count what a provider migration would import and write nothing; the job ends READY and is started with didit_session_manage_import.

face_templates.description: Build face templates from imported selfies and search them against the application's faces and blocklist (flags for review only). Requires lawful_basis_confirmed.

lawful_basis_confirmed.description: Confirms the customer has a lawful basis to share these selfies with Didit as processor. Only set it after the user states so.

tools.name: didit_session_list_import_providers
tools.description: List the 15 providers verifications can be migrated from: what each needs to connect (credential_fields, regions), whether its API can list records, the permissions its read-only key needs and its default status mapping.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

tools.name: didit_session_check_import_provider
tools.description: Read a provider with the customer's read-only key before creating a migration. Nothing is stored. For providers read by record IDs, pass record_ids (the first record ID of the export). The key is secret: never log or repeat it.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

application_id.description: Application id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

credentials.description: REQUIRED. SECRET. The provider's read-only key, named as its credential_fields.

record_ids.description: For providers read by record IDs: the first record ID of the export.

tools.name: didit_session_manage_import
tools.description: Act on an import job: start (a dry run that ended READY imports for real, with the status_mapping, face_templates and lawful_basis_confirmed sent now), pause, resume, cancel (what was imported stays; the uploaded file and the key are erased) or retry (runs an ended migration again as a NEW job with a new key in credentials, since the old one was erased; everything already in Didit is skipped).

tools.name: didit_workflow_edit_graph
tools.description: MODIFY an existing workflow's graph with small OPERATIONS - the right tool for editing a live workflow. You send only the deltas; the MCP fetches the full current graph SERVER-SIDE, applies your ops in order, validates, auto-creates a DRAFT (the live version is never touched), and saves. This means huge feature configs (documents_allowed, poa_documents_allowed, phone countries) are preserved exactly and you NEVER resend them. Validation failures return `applied:false` with the errors (nothing saved). The six op shapes are documented on the `operations` parameter; a typical edit upserts new nodes with set_node and rewires their neighbors with set_next. To branch after a feature node, point its `next` at a new branch node whose `branches` carry the rules (from didit_workflow_get_field_definitions) and whose goto targets are new status or feature nodes.

operations.description: Ordered edits applied to the full server-side graph. Each: one of — {op:'set_node', node_id, node:{…}} upsert a node; {op:'remove_node', node_id}; {op:'set_next', node_id, next:'<id|null>'} rewire a node's unconditional next; {op:'set_branches', node_id, branches:[…]} set conditional branches; {op:'merge_node_config', node_id, config:{…}, replace?} merge config keys (preserves the big allow-lists); a map value merges BY ENTRY (sent entries update/add, others are kept), arrays/scalars replace, replace:true replaces maps whole; {op:'set_start', start_node}.

Use this only to build a NEW/small workflow from scratch — to modify an EXISTING workflow prefer didit_workflow_edit_graph (you'd otherwise have to resend every node incl. multi-100KB allow-lists). If the workflow is published, a DRAFT is auto-created and the graph applied there (a live version is NEVER mutated); reviewable DRAFT unless `publish:true`. Validate first. Example graph: OCR → branch[ kyc.status==Declined → status(Declined); kyc.extra_fields.profession fuzzy_match 'Software Engineer' score 80 → DOCUMENT_AI(proof of funds) → status(Determine) ; else → status(Determine) ].

graph.description:
Node/branching workflow graph: { start_node, nodes }. `start_node` is the id of the entry node (must be a feature node). `nodes` maps nodeId → node. Node shapes: feature = {node_type:'feature', feature:<UPPERCASE, e.g. OCR|DOCUMENT_AI>, config?:{}, next?:<id>, branches?:[]}; branch = {node_type:'branch', branches:[{id, logic:'and'|'or', rules:[{field, operator, value, score?}], goto:<id>}], next?:<id fallback>}; status (TERMINAL) = {node_type:'status', session_status:'Approved'|'Declined'|'In Review'|'Determine'}. Branches are evaluated in order, first match wins; an empty rules:[] is the else/catch-all (kept last). Operators include `fuzzy_match` (string fields only, needs a `score` 0-100). Reference a feature's outcome with e.g. kyc.status / document_ai.status / bank.status, and an extracted value with kyc.extra_fields.profession. Each rule's `node_id` (the feature node that produces its field) is auto-filled for you — only set it (or use the `field@node_id` form) to disambiguate when the graph has several nodes of the same feature. Allow-list shorthands the MCP normalizes for you before saving: documents_allowed / poa_documents_allowed accept a doc-type array (["PASSPORT"] = passport-only, any country), doc NAMES (PASSPORT/ID/DRIVER_LICENSE/RESIDENCE_PERMIT) as well as codes (P/ID/DL/RP), scalar flags, and an "ALL" country key — every form becomes the canonical {ISO3:{CODE:{enabled:1}}}. poa_languages_allowed accepts a language array (["es"]) or a map ({"es":1}). Omit an allow-list to accept everything. KYC vs KYB: a graph is EITHER a person (KYC) workflow OR a business (KYB) workflow — never both, and the choice follows WHO is verified (a company → KYB, a person → KYC). A graph using any KYB feature (KYB_REGISTRY/KYB_DOCUMENTS/KYB_KEY_PEOPLE) may only also use DOCUMENT_AI, AML, QUESTIONNAIRE, PHONE_VERIFICATION, EMAIL_VERIFICATION, IP_ANALYSIS, BANK_VERIFICATION; it must NOT include person/KYC-only features (OCR, LIVENESS, FACE_MATCH, NFC, PROOF_OF_ADDRESS, DATABASE_VALIDATION, AGE_ESTIMATION). Company paperwork (incorporation, ownership, source of funds, business address) belongs in KYB_DOCUMENTS or DOCUMENT_AI on the KYB graph — never rebuild it as a KYC workflow. To verify the people behind a company (UBOs, officers, shareholders), build a SEPARATE KYC workflow and reference it from the KYB_KEY_PEOPLE node config (kyb_ubo_verification_workflow / kyb_officer_verification_workflow / kyb_shareholder_verification_workflow). tools.name: didit_questionnaire_create
tools.description: Create a custom questionnaire from an ordered list of questions. Send `title` + `form_elements` (an array of form-element objects, each with an UPPERCASE element_type) — NOT `questions`. The MCP assembles them into the questionnaire graph the backend stores (node ids and their ordering are derived here), so send the questions in the order the user should answer them and never build a graph yourself. Pass status:'draft' to keep it unpublished. A choice list longer than ~100 options does NOT fit in one call (the call is emitted token by token and gets cut off mid-JSON): create with status:'draft' carrying only the first ~100 choices, then add the rest with didit_questionnaire_append_choices in batches (its publish flag publishes with the final batch — a published questionnaire cannot be edited further).

Each: { element_type (uppercase, one of the allowed types), title (a plain string, or an object of locale→string e.g. {"en":"Your name"}), is_required (bool), placeholder (hint text), and for choice types a `choices` array }. A per-question hint goes in `placeholder`: `description` is only accepted on HEADING, SECTION_HEADER and PARAGRAPH elements.

Use it for long choice lists: create with the first ~100 choices, then append the rest here in batches of ~100 until the source list is exhausted, passing publish:true on the FINAL batch to publish. Choices the question already has (same value) are skipped, so retrying a batch never duplicates. Returns a compact summary whose total_choices is the stored count — verify against it instead of re-fetching the questionnaire.

tools.name: didit_org_get_balance
tools.description: Get current credit balance and auto-refill settings. Every check is billed from the first one: from 1 Nov 2026 an eligible Free organization gets $10 of monthly credit usable on any feature, paid plans carry their monthly plan credit (Growth $115, Scale $350), and no workflow is free of charge. The Free credit is decided per organization: `free_credit.receives` says whether this one gets it, and `free_credit.this_month` holds this month's credit, also once used up. `free_credit.eligibility` says why an organization does NOT get it, because the credit needs a work email: personal_email means it signed up with a personal email, temporary_email with a temporary one, company_exists that its company already has an organization, api_created that it was created through the API. Such an organization never had the credit, so it was not used up. Answer from these fields, never from the plan alone; when `free_credit` is absent, say you could not read it. Never answer a "not enough credits" report from this result alone: read the failing workflow with didit_workflow_list first - `is_white_label_enabled: true` adds $0.20/session, which is a common cause of credit running out faster than expected. This result also carries `allow_free_usage` (organizations on negotiated terms keep the monthly free allowance they were sold until renewal; false means that allowance is off for this organization) and `usage_summary.white_label_sessions`. When the balance cannot cover what the person wants to run, give them `next_steps.top_up_url` (the console top-up dialog with the amount filled in; replace the number to change it) or `next_steps.automatic_top_up_url` (save a card and turn on automatic top-up so the balance never runs out). Didit tools never charge a card. Meanwhile keep building in the organization's sandbox application (`mode: sandbox` in didit_context_get), which is never billed.

organization_id.description: Organization id (didit_context_get). Optional if you have only one.

tools.name: didit_org_top_up
tools.description: Top up credits ($50 to $20,000 per top-up). payment_method "checkout" (default) creates a Stripe Checkout page and returns checkout_session_url for the person to pay; it never charges a card by itself. payment_method "saved_card" charges the organization's saved primary card off-session, now, when a person turned on "Connected AI agents can top up with your saved card" in the Didit console (Billing > Payment methods; off by default; didit_org_get_balance shows it as agent_top_up.enabled where this tool is offered). It needs idempotency_key: choose ONE unique key per intended top-up (for example a UUID) and reuse that same key on any retry of that same top-up, so a retry can never charge twice; never reuse a key for another amount and never retry with a new key. A refusal carries `code`, `detail` and `next_step` {action, url, description}: agent_top_up_not_enabled (the switch is off), authentication_required (the card's bank asks the cardholder to approve), payment_method_required (no saved card) and card_declined are finished by the person: give them next_step.url (a Top up dialog link that says which agent asked, with the amount filled in).

payment_method.description: checkout (default): a Stripe Checkout page for the person to pay. saved_card: charge the organization's saved primary card now, only while a person has turned on the agent top-up switch in the console; requires idempotency_key.

idempotency_key.description: REQUIRED for payment_method saved_card (1 to 255 characters). One unique key per intended top-up; reuse the same key on any retry of that same top-up so the card is never charged twice. Ignored for checkout.

confirm.description: REQUIRED. Must be true. Only set after explicit user confirmation of this exact action: checkout creates a payment page, saved_card charges the saved card immediately.

tools.name: didit_verify_account_check
tools.description: Check that a bank account belongs to the person or company you name, before sending money to it. No session: send the name and the account, read the result. result is match, close_match, no_match or cannot_verify; on a close_match, holder_name is the name the bank holds the account under (when returned); account comes back masked to its last 4 characters. Billed once per check the bank answers at the account's country price, whatever the result (no_match and cannot_verify too); an error is never billed. Every call is a NEW billed check (no idempotency key, no read-back): do not retry blindly and store the response. Errors: 400 names the field and reason (consent required: in countries whose check needs the account holder's explicit consent, ask for it and send consent:true; nothing is billed); 402 top up; 404 country_not_covered or bank_not_covered; 503 the bank could not answer, send again later. Where Bank Verification is not switched on (production at the moment) it answers 404 bank_verification_not_available. A sandbox application calls no bank and charges nothing: the last 4 characters of the IBAN, else the account number, choose the answer (0001 close_match with holder_name, 0002 close_match without, 0003 and 0006 no_match, 0004 cannot_verify, 0005 a 503, 0009 a 400, anything else match).

account.description: REQUIRED. The account the way its country writes it: an iban, or an account_number with the bank or branch code the country needs (sort_code, routing_number, transit_institution, bsb, ifsc, bank_code, bic). Mexico takes a clabe and Argentina a cbu_cvu. A business account adds registration_id where the country asks. Spaces, dashes and dots are ignored; a key the country needs and does not get is a 400 that names it.
